title: client-usage-grain-and-proposal-stencils-mar-2026
text:
client-usage-grain-and-proposal-stencils-mar-2026

summary:
Working notes that translate raw customer threads into 'usage grains' (behavioral clusters) and then map each grain to compact proposal stencils and experiment probes. Goal: create repeatable micro-proposals product can execute quickly and measure impact on cost/latency/quality.

body:
Context: over the last 6 weeks CS collected ~120 threads tied to latency surprises, unexpected cost spikes, and model fallback behaviors. This doc groups those threads into usage grains (not personas) — lightweight behavioral patterns we can iterate on. Each grain has 1) customer signal excerpts 2) quick hypothesis 3) two proposal stencils (low-effort/medium-effort) 4) suggested probe experiment with success metrics. Notes are intentionally terse — use as handoff to product/eng for scoping.

Grain A — short chat spikes with transient 99th-percentile latency
- Signal: Several support tickets where customers running chat endpoints see occasional 20–30s spikes during concurrent onboarding flows. Mostly multi-turn, small token per-turn but many parallel sessions.
- Hypothesis: KV-cache warmups + small-batch scheduling collisions cause tail latency. Rare fallbacks to larger model variants exacerbate spikes.
- Proposal stencil (low-effort): expose "session-cache-warmup" flag on the SDK (default off) that allows sending a 1-token synchronous warmup call upon session creation; telemetry hook to correlate warmups with tail latency.
- Proposal stencil (medium-effort): scheduler isolation policy for low-latency chat sessions (soft reservation + pre-warm of KV slots). Requires runtime change + limited rollout.
- Probe experiment: run A/B across 5 pilot tenants (10% traffic) for 2 weeks. Metrics: 95/99/99.9 latency percentile, fraction of fallback model usage, error rate.

Grain B — embedding cost unpredictability with bursty indexing jobs
- Signal: Data engineering teams report sudden token/embedding bill jumps during nightly indexing that overlap with daytime inference. Jobs are heavy but short-lived; customers want predictable units.
- Hypothesis: shared host oversubscription + lack of per-tenant cost smoothing leads to transient price bumps.
- Proposal stencil (low-effort): recommend/automate AWS-style scheduled window for heavy batch jobs (document + quickstart); add a billing-estimate preview in Console for scheduled jobs.
- Proposal stencil (medium-effort): offer a "batch-capacity slot" product (time-boxed, lower unit price) as beta under Dedicated to absorb short bursts.
- Probe experiment: pilot with 3 customers; track cost variance (stddev of daily spend), and customer satisfaction CSAT.

Grain C — rollout/rollbacks and quality drift detection gaps
- Signal: A handful of customers had a model rollout that introduced subtle degradations (hallucination increase for a prompt family) which was not flagged by our existing QPS-based monitors.
- Hypothesis: current quality monitors are aggregate token-level metrics; they miss prompt-family regressions.
- Proposal stencil (low-effort): add a "prompt set guardrail" in Console where customers can attach 10–20 canonical prompts; run a lightweight diff on generation statistics after each deployment.
- Proposal stencil (medium-effort): integrate small-scale eval harness to run semantic similarity / factuality checks against stored gold labels and auto-rollback if degradation exceeds delta.
- Probe experiment: enable prompt-guardrail with 6 customers during an upcoming canary deploy; measure detection lead-time and false-positive rate.

Grain D — private deployment friction: KMS and audit log ergonomics
- Signal: Security teams using Private deployments report difficulty mapping Redwood's audit events to their SIEM schemas and granular KMS key rotation expectations.
- Hypothesis: mismatched naming conventions and missing mappings in the export transformer cause extra integration work.
- Proposal stencil (low-effort): publish a mapping doc + terraform module examples for common SIEMs.
- Proposal stencil (medium-effort): add an export transformer in Private that can be configured via YAML to rename fields and normalize timestamps.
- Probe experiment: create a one-week integration sprint with two pilot customers, measure integration hours saved.

Open assumptions/questions:
- We assume customers will accept marginal SDK flags for warmups; need to validate developer ergonomics.
- Cost smoothing for embeddings may cannibalize Dedicated revenue — product needs a revenue guard.
- Prompt guardrails require storage and privacy considerations if prompts contain PII (customer opt-in).

Quick decision notes: prioritize Grain A low-effort warmup flag + telemetry (reason: low eng cost, high potential tail latency reduction). Grain C prompt-guardrail is high business risk safety feature — mark for product sync.

Handoff checklist for Product/Eng:
- Product: scope warmup-flag API and Console toggle; write acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
- Eng (runtime): prototype session warmup path and add tracing hooks.
- CS: recruit pilot customers (we have 4 candidates) and prepare runbooks.
- DX/Docs: draft SDK sample and migration notes.

Appendix — exemplar customer excerpts (anonymized):
- "During onboarding we saw 1 in 300 sessions spike to 20s and the users churned out mid-flow."
- "Nightly embedding runs doubled our bill once; hard to correlate why."
- "We deployed model v2 and our summary quality dropped for our billing prompts; no alert fired."

decisions:
Short-term: implement warmup-flag telemetry + Console toggle (accept). Medium-term: schedule product/eng deep-dive for scheduler-isolation and prompt-guardrail evaluation.

probe_experiments:
Warmup flag A/B: 5 tenants, 2 weeks, metrics: 95/99/99.9 latency, fallback fraction
Batch-slot pilot: 3 tenants, measure cost variance and CSAT
Prompt-guardrail canary: 6 tenants during model rollout, measure detection lead time
Private SIEM transformer sprint: 2 customers, measure integration hours saved

prioritized_requests:
session-cache-warmup flag + telemetry (priority: P0 low-effort)
prompt-set guardrail in Console (priority: P1 medium-effort)
batch-capacity slot beta for Dedicated (priority: P2 product-econ review)
export-transformer for Private deployments (priority: P2 security-UX)
Console billing-estimate preview for scheduled jobs (priority: P3)
route-debugger traces per-request (candidate backlog)
kv-prefix-visualizer in Console (nice-to-have)
auto-rollback eval harness (architectural effort)
